newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, foreign ceiling raised.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, foreign ceiling raised.

text.p: Domestic institutional investors went on a selling spree, while foreigners selectively snapped up primary blue chips on Friday, the first day of a foreign share holding limit expansion, brokers said.
The ceiling rose to 23 percent from 20 percent.

"Foreign buying orders in selective blue chips exceeded expectations," said Choi Bum of C.S. First Boston. "But domestic institutional investors dumped their holdings and tried to reshuffle their investment portfolios."
The composite stock index rose 2.87 points to provisionally close at 706.10.
An official at the Korea Stock Exchange said a total of 42 shares had sold out to foreign investors, including favourites SK Telecom, POSCO, Samsung Electronics and Kookmin Bank.
The 42 included some stocks whose limit was reached before the expansion due to direct foreign investment or issuances of overseas equity-linked securities.
"The inflow of foreign funds helped increase market liquidity," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
Brokers forecast about 500 billion won would flow in with the expansion, but investors had anticipated more than that.

SK Telecom was the most preferred by foreign investors. The bid to share ratio for the nation's largest cellular phone operator was 118. But Kookmin Bank topped today's foreign buying volume list with 4.18 million shares.
Heavy institutional selling pressured blue chips. SK Telecom lost 29,000 won to 427,000 and Hyundai Motor shed 1,100 won to 22,400.

But POSCO and Samsung Electronics recouped early falls in the belief they had been undervalued. The steelmaker added 400 won to 54,000 and the chipmaker rose 700 won to 61,300, contributing to the major index closing higher.

Brokers said domestic institutional investors became liquid after profiting from blue-chip sales to foreigners. Brokers forecast low-priced large-capitalised shares would be the next target for institutions.
Daewoo Corp added 320 won to 6,150 and Kukje gained 400 won to 6,100.
Choi said the market would head for the 750 level with buying centred on cheap large-cap shares. "But the index will lose about 100 points after that."
Brokers said April's improved trade deficit contributed to more positive investor sentiment.
The shortfall narrowed to $1.5 billion from $2.04 billion a year earlier.
Brokers said some investors worried about margin loans exceeding customer deposits at brokerage houses by 10 billion won.
"As both favourable and negative factors were mixed in the market, I have to wait several days to see the future market direction," Kim of Dongsuh said.
Investors remained cautious about shares in the financially troubled Ssangyong and Jinro groups. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
